note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Classifier-layer bottleneck motivates pure low-precision training with peak-memory optimizations

nodes.name: Classifier layer is the XMC bottleneck
nodes.description: In extreme multilabel classification the linear classification head, rather than the encoder, dominates parameters and memory; with embedding dimension 768 and 3 million labels the weights alone take about 8 GiB, and about 32 GiB with gradients and optimizer states.

nodes.name: Renee fixes activation memory only
nodes.description: Renee computes classifier gradients directly without materializing the loss, which reduces activation memory and enables end-to-end training that beats negative-sampling approaches.

nodes.name: Renee mixed precision keeps extra copies
nodes.description: Renee's mixed-precision training keeps a full-precision parameter copy, a second FP16 copy of the classifier weights that persists for the whole step, and upcasts classifier gradients to FP32, inflating memory.

nodes.name: FP16 gradients are unstable at large label counts
nodes.description: Classifier-input gradient accumulation over the label dimension often overflows the FP16 range while classifier-weight gradients do not grow with label count, making Renee's training unstable and sensitive to encoder and label-space size.

nodes.name: Renee peaks at about 40 GiB
nodes.description: Renee's peak training memory is 39.7 GiB at 3 million labels, because the FP16 weight copy (4 GiB), gradients (4 GiB) and their FP32 upcast (8 GiB) stack up.

nodes.name: Pure BF16 training replaces mixed precision
nodes.description: ELMO uses BF16 instead of FP16 to avoid overflow because BF16 has the dynamic range of FP32, removing the extra high-precision copy of classifier gradients.

nodes.name: Naive BF16 updates stall training
nodes.description: Replacing 32-bit optimizer weights with BF16 weights stops training progress because round-to-nearest cancels updates smaller than half the gap to the next representable number.

nodes.name: Kahan summation and stochastic rounding compensate
nodes.description: ELMO uses Kahan summation for the encoder optimizer and stochastic rounding for the classifier optimizer to compensate for BF16 rounding error.

nodes.name: FP8 classifier works without scaling
nodes.description: Classifier weights can be trained in pure FP8 (E4M3) without loss scaling or mixed precision as long as gradients stay in BF16; 3 exponent bits suffice and mantissa degradation below 6 bits is recovered by stochastic rounding.

nodes.name: Chunking and fused kernel cut transient memory
nodes.description: Chunking the classifier update (3 to 8 chunks), decoupling encoder and classifier updates, and fusing classifier gradient computation with the optimizer step in a Triton kernel avoids storing classifier gradients and reduces peak memory.

nodes.name: ELMO memory for 3M labels
nodes.description: ELMO needs only 10.3 GiB (BF16) or 6.6 GiB (FP8) of peak memory for a 3-million-label model versus 39.7 GiB for Renee, a 4x-6x reduction.

nodes.name: Accuracy is preserved
nodes.description: ELMO's precision is comparable to Renee and competitive with existing XMC baselines on most public datasets despite pure low-precision training.

components.description: Low-precision training enables a new 8.6M-label benchmark

nodes.name: Public XMC benchmarks too small
nodes.description: The largest public XMC dataset has 3 million labels, so recent large-scale experiments used proprietary data.

nodes.name: LF-Paper2Keywords-8.6M dataset
nodes.description: The authors curate LF-Paper2Keywords-8.6M from DBLP-Citation-network V14, using paper titles and abstracts with keywords as 8.6 million labels.

nodes.name: Other XMC baselines do not scale to 8.6M
nodes.description: Other XMC baselines do not scale to 8.6 million labels, while ELMO's low-precision training yields significant memory and computational savings on it.

isolated_nodes.name: Wiki-500K memory
isolated_nodes.description: On Wiki-500K, Renee's peak memory is 105.64 GiB versus 18.8 GiB for ELMO BF16 and 9.02 GiB for ELMO FP8.

structural_reasoning: Argument moves from classifier-bottleneck and Renee's remaining memory/stability problems, to the pure BF16/FP8 recipe with compensation techniques, to measured memory and accuracy; the dataset contribution is a related branch.
